method.canonical: isolated tmux server; pane shell disabled echo, read one newline-terminated line, printed it between OUT markers; tmux send-keys -l supplied payload and a separate named Enter submitted it
method.raw: isolated tmux server; pane ran stty raw -echo and dd count=<payload bytes>; compared tmux send-keys -l with load-buffer from stdin plus paste-buffer; a second raw probe enabled bracketed-paste mode and verified -p -r framing

bracketed_multiline_result.method: one explicit bracket-open + UTF-8-safe 1000-byte load-buffer/paste-buffer -r chunks + bracket-close + named Enter
bracketed_multiline_result.wire_shape: ESC[200~ + paced body bytes with literal LF + ESC[201~ + CR

decision: Hold one bracketed-paste transaction open, feed it through a uniquely named tmux buffer in UTF-8-safe chunks of at most 1000 bytes with a 10ms pause, close the bracket once, then submit one named Enter.
rationale: Live clients disproved both simpler shapes: one unpaced paste lost a 16-byte block, while one bracketed paste per chunk intermittently inserted spaces at 1000-byte boundaries. The final single-bracket paced mechanism delivered the identical 6647-byte, 62-line body with SHA-256 2910388ffeafd86448ce8416476f02a8b5ed9fd19d040c839de4465731ae75c8 and zero diffs in hand-run OMP; the real-tmux regression preserves the same wire shape.
